args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. checkout-api was rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying, and review why v2.3.1 was promoted even though the RC was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's now passing health checks. I also opened a SEV2 incident, which paged on-call.

- **What went wrong:** All three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were running v2.3.1. It was failing health checks with an error rate of 18%. The test build of this version (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so that's the one I used. It needed no change-manager approval, because approval only applies to versions that have never been healthy in production.
- **After the rollback:** All three regions are on v2.3.0 and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) describes the failure, the rollback and the result. It lists two follow-ups: find out why v2.3.1 failed before redeploying it, and review why it went to production when the test build had failed in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
